title: Decca sessions of December 1941 and January 1942
summary: Why four sides were unissued and re-recorded; confusion over which titles exist.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Yes. This set here that begins with "Loch Lomond" and "Just Like A Gypsy", "My Blue Heaven", "St. Louis Blues" again, "When Your Love Has Gone", "My Ideal" -- now I don't have "The Night We Call It A Day" or "Concerto." They were -- Oh, I have "When Your Lover Has Gone" and "My Ideal" -- they were made on Decca.
Well, yes. But there is a -- there are two different recording sessions. It's a little complicated.
Yeah.
They were on -- In December of 1941, there were four sides cut, none of which were issued. That's the list of the four you mentioned -- "When Your Lover Has Gone", "My Ideal", "The Night We --
But I do have "When Your Love Is Gone" on that tape and "My Ideal."
That's right. You recorded
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
them again on the 28th of January of '42. And those were the two that were issued. So I have no idea why that would've been the case.
I don't either. Things got a little...
Perhaps something went wrong that day -- had technical problems.
I don't know. I really don't know.
This 'Concerto For Two' -- if I sang that, that I don't remember.
It may be in the Decca vault somewhere.
I see 'Lover Has Gone' and 'My Ideal' listed down here with this thing. Really, this whole thing, they never did it. I don't know.
Yeah. Well none of that set four actually came out.
Right.
'Cause I got 'Kentucky Babe' and 'My Curly Headed Baby.'
Okay. Those are missing from
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Yes.
And since I haven't -- Well, I have heard When Your Love Has Gone and My Ideal. And I believed there's no problem with the personnel on this thing.
No, I imagine it's the same.
